title: Choose BIDA's visual world
question: Each preview is the same screen: the Analyze postmortem (retention over beats, hook rewrite, the ten takes). Pick one, or re-roll.

options.label: Manila & Cartolina
options.lineage: the Filipino classroom report on manila paper and cartolina
options.thesis: Every postmortem reads like the report you once taped to the board: the drop circled in red Pentel.
options.viewport: Cartolina-blue rail (Brief, Ideate, Direct, Analyze); a manila analysis sheet with the retention line marker-drawn over the beat strip and the 0:02 drop circled in red; hook rewrite panel at right; takes T01-T10 along the bottom.
options.risk: Can tip into a school-project costume if the marker touches more than the chart and the circle.

raised.raise: The hook under review is set at display scale; every other label stays small, so the eye reads the words first.
The beat timeline sits on a visible half-second grid that the chart, beats and preview all snap to.
Pentel red is reserved for the one beat where viewers left; nothing else on screen is red.
Every take carries a code (T01-T10) and the take cards pack edge to edge in whole cells.

options.label: Komiks Weekly
options.thesis: A reel is a komiks strip: every beat is a panel, and the panel where readers stopped gets the balloon.
options.viewport: Beats drawn as a five-panel strip across the top with the retention curve in halftone under it; the drop panel flagged; hook rewrite and takes below.
options.risk: The most familiar 'storyboard as comic' idea; panels can crowd a working screen.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Each reel is a tape side: beats are tracks with running times that must fit the tape, Side A the original, Side B the rewrite.
options.viewport: Beat tracklist with right-aligned timecodes beside the retention line; a Side A / Side B flip between the original and rewritten hook.
options.case: Strong on clarity (timing budget, before/after flip); weaker on audience identification for 18-34 PH makers.
options.risk: Reads as nostalgia if the ballpoint spreads past the tracklist.

options.label: Warm Studio App
options.thesis: Soft cards and plain words; the one bright color is always something you can press.
options.viewport: Single column of cards: retention card, hook card, takes card; tangerine only on actions.
options.case: Holds product clarity; loses on audience identification and distinctiveness.
options.risk: Close to every creator app; little that says BIDA or the Philippines.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The hook as a giant specimen.
options.viewport: One giant hook line with axis-like sliders.
options.case: Loses both axes: little audience pull, hides the board.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale alone: the hook at display size.

options.label: Crouwel Grid
options.case: Loses both axes against a local world.
options.kept: A visible half-second grid under the timeline.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: The reel as a course; beats as controls.
options.viewport: Beats as numbered control circles on a course line.
options.risk: Nobody in the audience reads these maps.
options.kept: One ink reserved for the active problem only.

options.label: Con Catalog
options.thesis: Takes as a packed, coded thumbnail grid.
options.viewport: Ten takes as coded stamp cells, circled in biro.
options.risk: Too dense for the hero moment.
options.case: Loses both axes to the classroom report.
options.kept: Coded takes packed edge to edge in whole cells.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS board like Linear or OpusClip, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav, chart card, hook card, kanban of takes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competitors the judges have seen.
